# Task 4: Tournament Ranking Live Prediction

## Model

Based on the posterior predictive checks in Task 3, we extend the time-dependent Elo model from Task 2 by introducing a shared White-advantage parameter $w$. This extension addresses the most prominent discrepancy in the initial model while keeping the model relatively simple. We assign the prior

$$w\sim\mathcal N(0,50^2).$$

The expected score for White becomes

$$e=\frac{1}{1+10^{(R_B(t_c)-R_W(t_c)-w)/400}}.$$

All remaining priors and the three-outcome likelihood are retained from Task 2.

```{r}
# Get unique engine names
engines <- sort(unique(c(games$white, games$black)))

# Convert time controls into expected game duration
parts <- strsplit(games$timecontrol, "\\+")

tc <- vapply(parts, function(p) {
  as.numeric(p[1]) + 40 * as.numeric(p[2])
}, numeric(1))

# Standardize time control
tc_center <- mean(tc)
tc_scale <- sd(tc)
x <- (tc - tc_center) / tc_scale

# Encode outcomes
outcome_levels <- c("1-0", "1/2-1/2", "0-1")

# Prepare data for Stan
stan_data_task4 <- list(
  N = nrow(games),
  K = length(engines),
  white = match(games$white, engines),
  black = match(games$black, engines),
  outcome = match(games$result, outcome_levels),
  x = as.numeric(x)
)
```

```{r, results='hide'}
# Compile Stan model
mod_task4 <- cmdstan_model("helpers/task2_wa.stan")

# Sample from the posterior distribution
fit_task4 <- mod_task4$sample(
  data = stan_data_task4,
  seed = 42,
  iter_sampling = 1500
)
```

```{r}
# Posterior summary and MCMC diagnostics
summary_task4 <- fit_task4$summary(
  variables = c(
    "intercept", "slope",
    "white_advantage", "draw_tendency"
  )
)

# Display the shared parameters
knitr::kable(
  subset(
    summary_task4,
    variable %in% c("white_advantage", "draw_tendency"),
    select = c(variable, mean, sd, rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail)
  ),
  digits = 3
)
```

```{r}
# Check diagnostics across all parameters
cat("Max R-hat:", max(summary_task4$rhat), "\n")
cat("Min R-hat:", min(summary_task4$rhat), "\n")
cat("Min Bulk ESS:", min(summary_task4$ess_bulk), "\n")
cat("Min Tail ESS:", min(summary_task4$ess_tail), "\n")
```

The MCMC diagnostics indicate satisfactory sampling performance, with all R-hat values close to 1 and sufficiently high effective sample sizes. We therefore proceed with the extended model to predict the remaining tournament outcomes.

## Simulation

We estimate the probability that SchachMaus finishes among the top two engines using posterior predictive simulation. The tournament is played at a time control of 300+3, corresponding to an expected game duration of $t_c = 300 + 40 \cdot 3 = 420$ seconds.

We first load the observed tournament scores after the first two rounds and calculate the current total points for each engine. The observed tournament scores are treated as fixed starting values and are not used to update the model posterior.

```{r}
# Load observed tournament scores after two rounds
score_table <- read.csv(
  "../../../../data/task4_scores.csv",
  na.strings = ".",
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Calculate current total points for each engine
current_points <- rowSums(score_table[-1], na.rm = TRUE)
names(current_points) <- score_table[[1]]

# Match the order used in our Stan model
current_points <- current_points[engines]

cat("Current scores after two rounds:\n")
print(current_points)
```

Starting from these observed scores, we simulate the remaining three rounds (90 games) using posterior samples from our extended model.

For each simulation \(m\), we draw one joint sample of the model parameters from the posterior distribution and calculate the time-dependent rating of each engine at \(t_c=420\) seconds:

\[
R_j^{(m)}(420)=\alpha_j^{(m)}+\beta_j^{(m)}\frac{420-\overline{t_c}}{s_{t_c}}.
\]

Using these ratings and the corresponding White-advantage and draw-tendency parameters, we calculate the probabilities of a White win, draw, and Black win according to our extended model. The game outcomes are then randomly sampled from

\[
Y^{(m)} \sim \operatorname{Categorical}
\left(p_W^{(m)},p_D^{(m)},p_B^{(m)}\right).
\]

For each of the 15 engine pairings, we simulate three games with each color configuration, resulting in 90 remaining games. The simulated points are added to the observed scores, producing one possible final tournament ranking.

```{r}
# Time control for the tournament: 300+3
tc_tournament <- 300 + 40 * 3
x_tournament <- (tc_tournament - tc_center) / tc_scale

# Extract joint posterior samples
posterior_draws <- fit_task4$draws(
  variables = c(
    "intercept", "slope",
    "white_advantage", "draw_tendency"
  ),
  format = "draws_matrix"
)

# Simulate one possible continuation of the tournament
simulate_tournament <- function(draw_id) {

  # Select one joint posterior sample
  intercept <- as.numeric(
    posterior_draws[draw_id, paste0("intercept[", seq_along(engines), "]")]
  )
  
  slope <- as.numeric(
    posterior_draws[draw_id, paste0("slope[", seq_along(engines), "]")]
  )
  
  w <- posterior_draws[draw_id, "white_advantage"]
  d <- posterior_draws[draw_id, "draw_tendency"]

  # Ratings at tournament time control
  rating <- intercept + slope * x_tournament

  # Start with the observed scores
  points <- current_points

  # Every engine plays every other engine
  for (i in 1:(length(engines) - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):length(engines)) {

      # Three games per color configuration
      for (white in c(i, j)) {

        black <- if (white == i) j else i

        # Expected score for White
        e <- 1 / (1 + 10^(
          (rating[black] - rating[white] - w) / 400
        ))

        # Outcome probabilities
        p_draw <- 2 * d * e * (1 - e)

        probabilities <- c(
          e - 0.5 * p_draw,       # White wins
          p_draw,                 # Draw
          1 - e - 0.5 * p_draw   # Black wins
        )

        # Simulate three games
        white_points <- sum(sample(
          c(1, 0.5, 0),
          size = 3,
          replace = TRUE,
          prob = probabilities
        ))

        # Update scores
        points[white] <- points[white] + white_points
        points[black] <- points[black] + 3 - white_points
      }
    }
  }

  return(points)
}
```

We repeat this procedure 10,000 times, obtaining a distribution of possible final tournament outcomes.

```{r}
# Simulate 10,000 tournament continuations
set.seed(42)

n_sim <- 10000

draw_ids <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(posterior_draws)),
  size = n_sim,
  replace = TRUE
)

final_scores <- sapply(draw_ids, simulate_tournament)
```

## Results

### Top-2 Probability

We estimate the probability of SchachMaus finishing among the top two engines as the proportion of simulated tournaments in which SchachMaus achieves first or second place:

\[
\hat p_{\mathrm{top2}}=
\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}
\mathbf{1}\left(\operatorname{rank}_{SM}^{(m)}\leq 2\right),
\]

where \(M=10{,}000\) is the number of simulated tournaments. Since no tie-breaking rule is specified, tied engines are ranked randomly.

```{r}
# Determine SchachMaus' rank in each simulation
sm_id <- match("SM", engines)

sm_ranks <- apply(final_scores, 2, function(scores) {
  rank(-scores, ties.method = "random")[sm_id]
})

# Posterior predictive probability of finishing top two
p_top2 <- mean(sm_ranks <= 2)
```

Based on 10,000 posterior predictive tournament simulations, the estimated probability of SchachMaus finishing among the top two engines is `r round(100 * p_top2, 2)`%.

### Betting Decision

We now evaluate the proposed €100 bet. If SchachMaus finishes first or second, we gain €100; otherwise, we lose €100.

Using our estimated probability \(\hat p_{\mathrm{top2}}\), the expected net gain is

\[
\mathbb{E}[G]
=100\hat p_{\mathrm{top2}}-100(1-\hat p_{\mathrm{top2}})
=200\hat p_{\mathrm{top2}}-100.
\]

Thus, the bet has a positive expected gain if \(\hat p_{\mathrm{top2}}>0.5\).

```{r}
# Expected net gain from the bet
expected_gain <- 200 * p_top2 - 100

# Display results
results <- data.frame(
  `P(SM in top 2)` = round(p_top2, 4),
  `Expected gain (EUR)` = round(expected_gain, 2),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  results,
  caption = "Tournament Prediction and Betting Decision"
)
```

The expected net gain is €`r round(expected_gain, 2)`. Since this value is positive, we would accept the bet under a risk-neutral decision criterion.
